text.title: Dual-Write Shadow-Read Template — Output Contract
text.summary: The runbook is one JSON document with one section per rule in 01-core-rules.xml: per entity type the primary key, version field, parity exclusions and the numeric cutover gate; the dual-write path as a version-guarded upsert outside the old store's transaction with a durable retry queue and failure metric; the scheduled reconciliation job with its repair budget; the backfill ordered after dual-write and verified by counts and checksums; the shadow read that returns the old result, bounded by its own timeout and sampled by a runtime flag; four per-stage flags with their reverse order, a retention window and a rehearsed flip-back; and the named humans who approve the two production-affecting flips. Subagent MUST satisfy this contract before returning to caller.

required.field: the cutover the runbook governs (Postgres major upgrade, monolith-to-service split, schema rewrite)
the system of record until read cutover (r-old-store-authoritative)

per entity: primary_key, version_field, parity_excluded_fields, and the gate: mismatch_ratio_max, window_hours, min_comparisons — all written before shadow mode starts (r-dual-write-idempotent-writes, r-shadow-read-parity-diff, r-cutover-gate-numeric)

version-guarded upsert with compare-and-set, outside the old store's transaction, failures to a durable retry queue with dual_write_failures_total and an alert threshold (r-dual-write-idempotent-writes, r-old-store-authoritative)
named scheduled job, cadence, max repairs per run, reconciliation_repairs_total, declared before dual-write is enabled (r-reconciliation-job-required)
starts after dual-write, uses the same upsert, verified by per-partition counts and checksum before any parity number (r-backfill-before-shadow)

normalising comparator, returns the old store's result, candidate timeout at or under the old p99, exceptions swallowed and counted, runtime sampling flag starting under 100 percent, shadow_read_mismatch_ratio with retained samples (r-shadow-read-parity-diff, r-shadow-read-no-user-impact)
four per-stage runtime flags, the reverse order, retention window for old-store writes, flip-back rehearsed before write-to-old is turned off (r-rollback-flag-per-stage)
gate declared before shadow; the gate evaluation URL and named approvers for read-from-new and write-to-old-off (r-cutover-gate-numeric; human checkpoint)
URLs: reconciliation dashboard, backfill verification, gate evaluation at cutover, flip-back rehearsal

forbidden.pattern: dual_write.upsert_kind other than version-guarded-upsert, or compare_and_set_on_version false (fm-non-idempotent-fanout)
dual_write.outside_old_store_transaction false, or failures that propagate to the user request (fm-new-store-fails-request)
no reconciliation job, or a cadence of monthly or longer, or declared_before_dual_write false (fm-no-reconciliation)
backfill.starts_after_dual_write false, uses_same_upsert false, or parity reported before counts and checksum matched (fm-backfill-clobbers-live)
shadow_read.comparator raw, or an entity with no parity_excluded_fields declared (fm-parity-noise)
shadow_read.returns_old_store_result false, no candidate timeout, or sampling_percent_initial of 100 (fm-shadow-read-latency)
a single combined migrated flag, retention_window_days under 1, or write-to-old off before the flip-back was rehearsed (fm-old-store-dropped-early)
cutover.gate_declared_before_shadow false, or read_from_new flipped without an evaluation URL and a named approver

allowed-transformations.transformation: Where an entity type has no natural version column, derive the version from the change-data-capture log sequence number and name it as version_field.
Group entity types that share a table family under one entry when their key, version field and gate are identical; list the members in name.
Express the candidate timeout as a measured old-store p99 at runbook time; re-measure and update it when shadow sampling is raised.

list.item: Every entity type names its primary key, version field, parity exclusions and a numeric gate (ratio, window, minimum comparisons) written before shadow mode.
Dual writes are version-guarded upserts outside the old store's transaction; a failed new-store write is queued and counted, never surfaced to the user.
A named reconciliation job runs at least weekly with a repair budget and was declared before dual-write went on.
Backfill started after dual-write, used the same upsert, and matched per-partition counts and checksum before any parity number was reported.
Shadow reads return the old store's result, time out at or under the old p99, swallow and count exceptions, and are sampled by a runtime flag starting under 100 percent.
Four distinct runtime flags with the reverse order recorded; old-store writes continue through the retention window; the read flip-back was rehearsed before write-to-old goes off.
read-from-new was flipped only with a linked gate evaluation and a named approver; write-to-old-off has its own named approver.
